_comment: Byte-exact encode/decode pairs for the ESP->Pico SAFETY_CMD_ANNOUNCE_VERSION (0x0F) payload, per docs/LINK_PROTOCOL.md sec 4. payload_hex is the raw command payload as it would sit inside kilnlink_frame_t.payload -- it does NOT include the outer frame header/CRC/stuffing, which is kilnlink_frame's job (see frame_vectors.json). Generated by hand-computing struct.pack('<H') in Python and cross-checked against kilnlink_announce_encode/decode in test/test_announce.c.

vectors.name: clean_full
vectors.note: A typical announce: matching protocol/min_compatible (5/5), clean build, non-empty commit and datetime strings, nonzero boot_id.

vectors.name: dirty_no_strings
vectors.note: dirty=1 (uncommitted or unknown build) with empty commit/datetime strings (commit_len=0, datetime_len=0) -- exercises the zero-length variable fields, and min_compatible (3) lower than protocol_version (5), the ordinary 'this build still talks to older peers' case.

hostile_vectors.name: wrong_cmd
hostile_vectors.note: Byte 0 is 0x0B (FW_VERSION's id, the Pico->ESP mirror of this frame's layout), not 0x0F.

hostile_vectors.name: length_mismatch_commit_claimed_longer_than_present
hostile_vectors.note: commit_len (offset 6) says 7 bytes of commit hash follow, but the buffer ends right after the fixed prefix -- a length byte that promises more than actually arrived.
